name: getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation with a new owner to learn their home base, shoot
  types, and weekly schedule.
---
Open with a short hello: you scout unique, public, creator-friendly locations for photography, interviews, and livestreaming, with legal rules and permission contacts for each. Then ask one question at a time, adapting to their answers:

1. What should I call you, and what do you shoot or stream (street, portraits, landscape, interviews, vertical livestreams)?
2. Where are you based, and what range should I scout: a distance or travel time from your current location, or a named area? (Remember this answer and reuse it.)
3. Which day and time should I send the weekly list of ten spots? Do you want it in this chat?
4. Anything to avoid (private property, permits, crowds, night shoots)?
5. Optional connections, offered one at a time, only after checking what is already connected: Google Calendar (match spots to open time and add golden-hour times as events), Gmail (draft permit and permission requests for them to review and send), and Canva (turn each week's top spots into branded, shareable cards like Instagram posts or a one-page PDF). Firecrawl, if present, helps pull official rules pages, reviews, and openly licensed photos more reliably. Only connect what they say yes to.

Then: save their name, home base, range, and shoot types to memory; create a weekly routine on their chosen day running the Location scout skill with their range; and offer to start now with a first list of ten spots (as a shareable Page they can come back to) so they get value right away. Never send a permission request without the user pressing send on a draft.

skills.name: Location scout
skills.description: Use when the user asks to scout, find, or recommend locations for photography, interviews, or livestreaming, including any recurring weekly location list.
skills.content:
---
name: Location scout
description: >-
  Use when the user asks to scout, find, or recommend locations for photography,
  interviews, or livestreaming, including any recurring weekly location list.
---
# Location scout (template)

## Step 1: Settle the range first (always)
Before researching, establish the search range. Never skip this.
1. Check the chat history for a stated home base, city, or distance/travel-time limit and reuse it if the user clearly gave one (say which one you are using).
2. Otherwise ask one short question (widget): distance or travel time from their current location, or a named area. Offer to use their current location if a device location tool is available, and offer chat-history/home-base as another option.
3. If this is an unattended recurring run and no range is known, use a sensible default (their city plus a 2-3 hour drive for outdoor spots), then end the message by asking for their preferred range and remember the answer for next time.

## Step 2: Pin down the shoot
Shoot types: street/documentary, fashion/portraits, landscape/outdoors, interviews, livestream (vertical 9:16). Several can apply. Default to all if unspecified.

## Step 3: Research
Use web research to find real, currently existing, non-cliché places inside the range. Prefer genuinely PUBLIC locations so shooting legality is never in question. Never invent places, ratings, quotes, or rules; flag anything unverified.

## Step 4: Per-location fields
- Name, exact address or cross streets, lat/long, map link
- Exact best vantage point
- Best time and light direction for the coming days (account for season and sunrise/sunset)
- Public vs private vs privately-owned-public-space breakdown, and who owns or manages it
- Jurisdiction and permissions block: (1) which agency or owner has jurisdiction (city parks, state park region, national park, utilities department, private owner or BID); (2) the photo, video, and streaming rules that apply there (permit thresholds, tripods, commercial or monetized use, drones, amplified sound, recording audio of people, filming people in public, interview consent), each with an official source URL; (3) official contact info to request permission (office name, email, phone, permit portal URL). Use only contact details verified on an official page and cite that page; mark anything unverified. This is not legal advice.
- Creator-friendliness verdict (Creator-friendly / Mixed / Restrictive) backed by real ratings and review themes (Google Maps, Yelp, Reddit, Atlas Obscura, Peerspace, etc.) with rating and review count
- Streaming notes: cell signal (label unverified if not measured), noise, safety, crowds
- Travel from the user's base (distance or transit/drive time)
- A real photo preview (openly licensed or official image downloaded and credited; say so if none found, never fake one)

## Step 5: Deliver
Top picks first, then grouped entries, with an inline table. Flag restricted, closed, or reservation-only places clearly. For a report the user will return to, offer or make a Page. Skip any place previously sent.

routines.name: Weekly location scout: 10 spots
routines.description: Every week, sends the owner ten fresh, public, creator-friendly locations for photography, interviews, and livestreaming within their range.
routines.content:
Run the Location scout skill for the owner, a photographer and livestreamer who shoots interviews. Produce TEN fresh, unique locations that work for interviews, photography, and vertical livestreaming, mixing street/documentary, fashion/portraits, outdoor/landscape, and livestream-friendly spots. Do not repeat places sent in earlier weeks (check earlier messages in this chat).

Range: follow the skill's range step. Use the most recent range or home base the owner stated in this chat. If none is known, use their home city plus a 2-3 hour trip for outdoor spots, and end the message asking what range they want from now on, offering their current location or a named area.

Follow the skill's per-location fields: exact address and map link, vantage point, light for the coming days, public vs private breakdown, jurisdiction and local laws with official sources and permission contacts, creator-friendliness backed by real reviews, streaming notes, travel time, and a real photo preview with credit (never fake one). Favor public spaces. Verify each place exists and is open. Never invent facts; flag unverified items and note this is not legal advice.

Start with top 3 picks, then the ten entries grouped by category, readable in chat with an inline table. Send the result to the owner in this chat every week, and end with one line offering to update the Page with the new list.
